# Exact optimal exit cost over an entire globally critical menu
EVERY globally critical cap at its deepest point, including every
continuous normal. It proves that the attained selection theorem cannot
unconditionally make the reciprocal exit cost equal to one, or bound it
by an absolute constant independent of continuous dimension. The source
has depth strictly above OC, arbitrarily close to its sharp threshold.

## 1. Actual convex family and exact global depth

Let d>=2, let T be a d-simplex of volume one with one vertex at the
origin, and let lambda_0,...,lambda_d be its barycentric coordinates,
where lambda_0(0)=1. Write

    gamma=(d/(d+1))^d,     b=1/(d+1),
    A=epsilon T,          a=epsilon^d.

Choose 0<a<rho_d, where rho_d>0 is the proved dimension-only threshold
in `candidate 1d1be0b22c707856`. In
particular rho_d<=((d-1)/(d+1))^d<1, so 0<epsilon<1.

Take the actual lifted convex hull with fibers A,T,T at bases -1,0,1.
Its only integer fibers are exactly these three. The cited complete
all-halfspace theorem gives the unique deepest point (0,g), g the
centroid of T, and exact raw depth

    Q=gamma+a.                                         (1)

Its total mixed mass is M=2+a. The dependence on that audited theorem
is explicit; nothing in this note estimates depth by a finite normal
screen.

## 2. Classification of every globally critical through-point cap

Every critical halfspace through (0,g) is exactly of the form

    H_(i,L)={lambda_i(x)-Lz>=b},
          0<=i<=d,       L>=1-b=d/(d+1).              (2)

Positive rescaling of its defining inequality does not change the cap.
There are no other critical continuous directions or vertical caps.

Here is the proof. A vertical through-point cap contains the full middle
fiber and one endpoint, so its mass is at least 1+a>Q. For a nonvertical
cap let u be its continuous direction. In the notation of the cited
profile theorem, write f(u) for its own centroid cap fraction on T and
q(u) for the reflected-threshold tail fraction. For every coupled tilt,
that theorem proves

    cap mass >= f(u)+min(a,q(u)),
    f(u)>=gamma,
    f(u)-gamma+q(u)>=rho_d>a.                          (3)

If q(u)<a, (3) gives strict mass above gamma+a. Otherwise equality
of the actual cap mass with Q forces f(u)=gamma. The ordinary simplex
equality characterization therefore makes u one of the canonical
vertex directions lambda_i. Its through-g equation is then uniquely
written lambda_i(x)-Lz>=b for a real L.

Let m_i=min_A lambda_i>=0. At the left fiber the threshold is b-L;
at the right fiber it is b+L. If L<b-m_i, the right threshold is
strictly less than 2b-m_i<=2b. Its right T cap therefore has mass at
least (1-2b)^d>a, already more than the entire allowed endpoint
budget a. If L>=b-m_i, the left A is fully captured, so equality
requires the right T cap to have zero volume. This is equivalent to
b+L>=1, or L>=1-b.

Conversely L>=1-b implies L>=b-m_i, because d>=2 and m_i>=0.
Thus A is fully captured, the right T cap has zero volume, and the
middle canonical cap has mass gamma. Its exact total mass is Q.
This proves the complete menu classification (2), including supporting
boundary traces and the minimal allowed tilt.

## 3. One exact residual optimizer and its retained KKT row

Use the finite cap cover consisting of the critical canonical caps

    P_i={lambda_i(x)-2z>=b}

and the caps isolating the right endpoint

    Q_i={lambda_i(x)+2(z-1)>=b},       0<=i<=d.

Their budgets are respectively Q and gamma. Their one-cap residual
minimum roots are

    (e_-1,e_0,e_1)=(0,c,c),
    c=(1-gamma)^(1/d).                                (4)

The unique optimal sampled convex threshold is h_-1=h_0=h_1=c.
Indeed h_0>=c and h_-1+h_1>=2h_0 imply a sum of dth powers at least
3c^d, with equality only at those equal values. They satisfy all
obstacle constraints, so this lower bound is attained.

With s=d c^(d-1), choose the exact KKT multipliers

    mu_(0,-1)=mu_(0,1)=s,
    lambda_0=3s,         lambda_-1=lambda_1=0.

The martingale coupling has pi_(0,j)=s for every j in {-1,0,1}.
Its single nonzero normalized row assigns weight 1/3 to each base.

Adjoining ANY member of (2) to this finite cover gives a cap with
source residual root c, fully captures the left endpoint,
and captures zero d-volume at the right endpoint. At the minimal tilt
the latter trace is its canonical vertex, rather than the empty set.
At the middle fiber it is
again a canonical cap of mass gamma. Consequently all three residual
obstacle values, the unique optimizer, and these exact KKT data are
unchanged. The original cover is retained. One may also replace P_i
by a member of (2) with the SAME canonical direction i, since its
trace measure on every measured fiber is identical. Setwise coverage
is retained by the full left fiber, the unchanged middle canonical
cap cover, and the retained Q_i cover at the right fiber. The classification
therefore optimizes over a genuine KKT-preserving critical menu,
not merely an arbitrary class of cuts. Replacing one direction by
a different direction and discarding the original cap is not used
as a coverage-preserving operation.

## 4. Exact first exits and the optimal reciprocal cost

For -1<=z<=0, writing z=-t, the actual continuous section is

    C_-t=[1-(1-epsilon)t]T,      0<=t<=1.               (5)

The inclusion A subset T shows that allowing a contribution from the
+1 fiber can only increase the homothety coefficient of A and shrink
the section, so (5) describes the actual lifted hull exactly. For
0<=z<=1 the section is T.

For a canonical direction i>=1, the minimum of lambda_i on every
section in (5) is zero. The strict residual of H_(i,L) on that
section exists exactly while b-Lt>0. Hence its first exit toward
the left destination is

    t_- = b/L,          s_-:=1/t_-=(d+1)L.             (6)

For the direction i=0, the minimum is (1-epsilon)t, so instead

    t_- = b/(L+1-epsilon),
    s_-=(d+1)(L+1-epsilon).                           (7)

In every canonical direction the entire segment toward the right
destination has positive residual: the threshold is b+Lt>=b and
the section remains T. That exit fraction is 1, as is the self
destination at the source.

Therefore the normalized KKT row's exact reciprocal correction is

    C_(i,L)=(s_-+2)/3.

By (2), every critical L is at least d/(d+1). Equations (6)--(7)
give the exact minimum over the ENTIRE critical menu:

    min_(critical H through (0,g)) C(H)=(d+2)/3.        (8)

It is attained by every i>=1 at L=d/(d+1). In the direction i=0
the best cost is larger by (d+1)(1-epsilon)/3. Thus changing
continuous directions cannot improve (8).

The selected maximal CLOSED residual projection on the row interval
is exactly [-1/d,1]. The strict/positive residual projection is
(-1/d,1]. Every other critical cap has a smaller or equal closed
projection; in this example the attained selection theorem genuinely
finds the optimal projection as well as the optimal scalar cost.

## 5. Consequences and exact scope

The optimum in (8) is strictly above one for every d>=2 and tends
to infinity with d. Thus neither global criticality, preservation of
the exact residual KKT row, nor optimization over ALL critical caps
gives an unconditional dimension-free bound on this exit correction.
For example, for d>=7 the optimum is at least 3, while
1/gamma_d=(1+1/d)^d<e<3. Hence even a proposed upper bound 1/gamma_d
is false in this genuine critical class.

The fully captured destination volume is a=epsilon^d and tends to
zero; the row hitting weight remains 1/3. The optimum (8) does not
change. This rules out charging that hitting weight or its reciprocal
exit cost solely by a fixed multiple of the captured destination
volume, even after the best possible critical-cap selection.

Nevertheless this is strictly an ABOVE-target family:

    Q/M-gamma/2 = a(2-gamma)/[2(2+a)] >0.               (9)

That positive gap tends to zero as a tends to zero, while (8) remains
unchanged. Thus an ordinary near-sharp or small-gap argument by itself
does not make these exit corrections vanish. A mechanism using the
strictly below-OC premise, a different charging invariant, or a
sharper comparison than this stopped-root cost remains logically
possible. None is asserted by the present certificate.

In fact the ORIGINAL row's residual roots are (0,c,1), and their
unchanged average is (c+1)/3<c, because c=(1-gamma)^(1/d)>1/2.
Thus this family does not obstruct the unmodified row's root inequality
or every possible volume charge. The unavoidable factor (d+2)/3 belongs
specifically to the geometric first-exit reweighting. Its excess and
fixed hitting weight cannot be paid solely by a fixed multiple of the
vanishing captured destination volume; that is the precise obstruction.

For a fully rational planar calibration, d=2 and epsilon=1/10 satisfy
the strict profile range: rho_2=2(sqrt(10)-3)/9>1/100. Then

    Q=409/900, M=201/100, h^2=5/9,
    optimal tilt L=2/3, optimal exit fraction=1/2,
    optimal reciprocal correction=4/3.

Every number in this last display is exact. The sufficient profile
inequality follows by squaring 3+9/200<sqrt(10), so no numerical
approximation is needed.
